specification: Epic: Widget names are case- and whitespace-insensitive: the store keeps each name normalised (trimmed, lower-case), and a client can always look a widget up by the name it created it with, in any case or spacing. Widgets record their creation time.

findings.Rule: ticket-requirement: lookup by name in any case or spacing
findings.Message: The by-name route passes the raw URL segment to FindByName, which per docs/plans/EPIC3-B.md is an ordinal, case-sensitive comparison with no normalisation, so GET /widgets/by-name/ALPHA or a padded name returns 404 even though the widget was created as "Alpha", violating the ticket's requirement that lookup works in any case or spacing.

findings.Snippet: returns the first widget whose `Name` equals `name` under an ordinal, case-sensitive comparison (`string.Equals(..., StringComparison.Ordinal)`)
findings.Message: The plan makes FindByName case-sensitive and unnormalised, so a client cannot find a widget by the name it was created with in any case or spacing, which the ticket requires; the plan's own test asserting FindByName("ALPHA") returns null contradicts the ticket.

The by-name route passes the raw route value to FindByName without trimming or lower-casing it, so lookups by mixed-case or padded names will return 404 as required by the ticket's case- and whitespace-insensitive lookup.

findings.Snippet: public record Widget(int Id, string Name, DateTimeOffset CreatedAt);
findings.Message: Adding a required third positional parameter breaks any existing two-argument `new Widget(...)` call sites, and the plan admits the grep for them was denied and the integration test file was not read, so the change may not compile.

findings.Snippet: returns the first widget whose `Name` equals `name` under an ordinal, case-sensitive comparison (`string.Equals(..., StringComparison.Ordinal)`)
findings.Message: The plan specifies a case-sensitive FindByName, which violates the epic requirement that a client can look a widget up by its creation name in any case or spacing, and the plan's own test asserts FindByName("ALPHA") returns null.

findings.Snippet: public record Widget(int Id, string Name, DateTimeOffset CreatedAt);
findings.Message: Adding a required CreatedAt parameter breaks any existing two-argument `new Widget(...)` call site, and the plan admits these call sites were not checked.

findings.Snippet: returns the first widget whose `Name` equals `name` under an ordinal, case-sensitive comparison (`string.Equals(..., StringComparison.Ordinal)`)
findings.Message: FindByName is specified as case-sensitive and does not trim input, so a client that created "Alpha" (stored as "alpha") gets a 404 from /widgets/by-name/Alpha, which breaks the ticket's requirement to look up by the creation name in any case or spacing.

findings.Snippet: returns the first widget whose `Name` equals `name` under an ordinal, case-sensitive comparison (`string.Equals(..., StringComparison.Ordinal)`)
findings.Message: The ticket requires a client to look up a widget by the name it was created with in any case or spacing, but this plan makes FindByName case-sensitive and does not normalise the query, so FindByName("ALPHA") returns null and the new by-name route cannot satisfy the epic.

The route passes the raw path segment to FindByName without trimming or lower-casing, so a lookup such as "  Alpha " will miss a widget stored as "alpha" even though the ticket requires any case or spacing to work.
